Let's start out with a couple of caveats. We're not going to be talking about settings here. We're going to be

accessible and focused on QOL and optimization changes you can make inside the game. So without any further ado,
let's get into the first setting you should change, turning on gravestone protection.
This setting is critical if you are playing with other players. When you die in Dragonwilds, you leave behind a
gravestone that contains everything you were carrying when you died aside from your equipped gear. So be a real pain if
someone just logged into your server and sniped all your gear while you're on a death run to come get it. By toggling
gravestone protection on, this prevents other players from accessing your gravestone. So if you do die, this will
at least protect you from adding insult to injury, making sure you'll be able to reclaim your gear once you eventually
hobble back to the point where you died. The only reason you might not want to have gravestone protection on is if
you're playing with people you trust and you're planning on asking them to bring
your gear back to base for you. So there are some circumstances where this should
be on, some where it should be off, but generally I'd recommend putting gravestone protection on by default and
only turning it off if you need to. You can actually turn it off after you've died too. If someone you were
adventuring with is still in the area where you died and you don't want to have to hoof it all the way back by yourself.
Next we're going to talk about screen shake. This generally adds immersion to the game, makes fights seem more real.
It makes the image on your screen shake around a little bit when you're hit by enemies or in bosses use huge attacks.
But screen shake can also be distracting and get in the way. When you're laser focused on a boss fight for instance,
when you're trying to avoid mechanics and get all the damage in you can during a damage phase, generally though to make

tree and all the logs fly into your inventory, that's because they've been magnetized due to this setting here,
auto magnetize world items. Generally, I find this setting to be really useful. It doesn't grab anything you haven't
looted yet. So for instance, if you've not yet interacted with a stone node on the ground, it won't just pull that
stone to you automatically. But for anything you've already interacted with, that includes items you've logged or
mined, those will automatically go into your inventory if this is on. And I generally recommend keeping it on. You
might want to turn it off though if you're low on inventory space or you're going through an area where you don't
need the items. Basically, it's just good to know this one's here, even though you'll probably want to keep it
on by default no matter what. The next one though is a bit more up to interpretation. You can also choose
whether to auto magnetize items that are produced by your crafting stations. And honestly, this one sometimes gets
annoying. So for instance, in my house, I built my grills right next to my loadstone. So that means if I set
something to grill and then port back in my base, all my grilled items will automatically flood in my inventory.
Also, while you're working at one crafting station, you might not want items from other crafting stations just
plugging up your inventory automatically. I generally keep this setting on, but I totally understand if

really like the hair and the face style you chose at character creation, you can
